My wife and I arranged to meet our daughter downtown for lunch at the newly opened restaurant. Set at the corner of Market Street and Meridian, the main entrance is found on Market about half a block west of Monument Circle. For long time Indy residents, you may recognize the former Blocks Department store. The restaurant only uses a small portion of the once huge department area. The scale here is much smaller without the opulent decor of the previous tenant. Upon entering, you see the small dining area and bar. Additional seating is outside on the expanded sidewalk area. There was table side service, but the waitress was also the hostess and worked behind the counter too, so there were some times when it was difficult to find any staff in the dining room if we needed assistance. The music was cranked way too loud for the small dining area though I will compliment the staff for making an adjustment suitable to make our dining conversation possible. Despite the small number of staff working, the food was delivered properly and without much delay. I thought it was seasoned well, but did find that the two dishes ordered with chicken were cooked too long and seemed dry. I was able to try some of my daughter's shrimp skewer and enjoyed IT. Not rubbery, just a pleasant bite. The prices were higher than most of the downtown options) nd the wait could be improved to be competitive so that diners aren't pressured to leave just to make it back to work on time. If you are downtown within walking distance, I recommend that option on nice days. Some street parking was available and some parking garages aren't too far away, but on the day I went the doors to the garages in the building weren't working. So allow plenty of time for traffic and finding a spot.

It has a postage stamp size dining area with only 2 tables for eating in, and 3 chairs for waiting on take away. The space is still clean and the kitchen shiny, as it has been open little more than a week. The menu is extensive and basically a traditional Chinese/American emporium. Nothing authentic, but if you wanted really good Chinois you would not be parking your wheels on S. Broad in the first place. My Orange Flavored Chicken was a load in the styro container they give to even those who eat in. The chicken was fresh enough, and had not been deeply frozen. The sauce was gloopy orange colored, although the taste of the citrus was weak, despite the orange peel in the mix. The Fried Rice was a bright yellow from the dye used in the bullion stock that morning. It had plenty of roast pork and veggies in it, but I did not see much (if any) egg scrambled into it. The people here are Fuzhounese, the province just north of old Canton, and across the straits from Taiwan. Their cuisine is similar to Cantonese, but has some other influences. It tends toward less sweetness, but close enough to allow for success in the Chinese take out wars. If you are interested, go soon while everything is new and clean. The owners are there and take an interest in getting things right. Just remember what you are dealing with, and you will not be disappointed.

The owners and chef are legit from Hanoi, and know their way around a Vietnamese kitchen. No excuses necessary! I was in the mood for their version of wonton soup, which was basically pho broth with a large number of dumplings rather than noodles in the hot bath. Same accoutrements (Thai basil, sprouts, jalapeno slices, lime wedge), and same great taste, but with beef/pork stuffed wontons. Why not five star? Well, because I am spoiled by visiting Vietnam and eating incredible food in both the north and south of the country. The small houses in Philly and Ocean Grove, California are often excellent, and this one may yet transport me to the Mekong River as those do. When that happens there will be five stars shining above its door. Bravo to Bravo for being as slurpin' good as it is!

If you don't mind paying $23 for a four pack of local suds, Newtown Brewery is a worthwhile destination for the yeast heads in the crowd. The facility is very attractive with plenty of wood and stone, and the beer is excellent for the most part. We stopped in last weekend and the room was hopping. Tables full of folks escaping Covid captivity. But, we weren't ready for a space packed with over a hundred people without masks, nor social separation, so we bought our "I lost My Marbles" Belgian Tripel four can and headed home. Just didn't feel safe (and thus the one star deduction for lack of public awareness by management). Under better circumstances, Newtown Brewing would be a big hit in these parts, and in fact it appears it already is. The beer was quite strong at 11% alcohol content, but the taste was great, and the color a robust rusty slurry. Liked it a lot. They do have a food truck in the parking lot most weekends, and we were fortunate to approach the window of Stuff'd Bunns and grab two sliders to partake with the ale at home. More on them in a separate review coming soon to these Yelp pages. I hate to have to take out a loan to support my occasional beer addiction, but aside from that, and the insensitivity to the CDC guidelines, Newtown Brewery really enhances the neighborhood. Just hope no one gets exposed to the virus. That is a price far to high to pay for a momentary pleasure.

I enjoyed my visit to Deviate Brewing. The interior is a bit crowded and dark compared to a number of a number of breweries I have visited, but the bartender was friendly enough and mentioned a couple brews that were available even though they weren't listed on the chalkboard behind the counter. I decided to go with a flight (4 five ounce selections) which have varying prices depending upon the brews selected (anywhere between $8-14 for the four choices). Lots of Stouts and IPA's are featured. The four I chose were full flavored and I enjoyed 3 out of 4. The PB&C, a peanut butter imperial stout was full flavored and was quite good as a special choice. The Color Blind (blonde stout 7.8%) was another smooth and full flavored choice. I also enjoyed the Kuppa Kopi (coffee porter 5.7%) for its smooth coffee taste without the bitterness. I would drink each of these again! My only choice that didn't taste quite so appealing was the Victimless Crime, an oatmeal stout orange zest. Something about it seemed like an odd pairing the more I drank.

I don't know. Maybe I'm a snob when it comes to oysters and seafood in general, but I was left underwhelmed by my experience at this chain. My friends ordered a dozen oysters; half raw and half char broiled. I ordered the seafood etouffee. I tried the oysters, but I immediately noticed that they weren't very big. The char broiled oysters were good and had a nice buttery flavor. My etouffee was ok, but not really anything special. The prices here seem a little bit steep for what seems to be just a casual dining place. I will say that one of my friends ordered the seafood platter, which came with fried crab, catfish, oysters and fries. It was huge, looked really good, and can definitely be split between two people. The service was good and we were seated quickly, with only about a ten minute wait. Given the choice, I would be more inclined to support a small local business, rather than this chain.
